summary: This excerpt from a fiction book (Book 4, part 104) follows Valentine and her friends after a revolution that began when zombie-related drug prices led to the overthrow of the government. The narrator describes how the revolution is taught through a game, recalls the violent ouster of the PM, and then depicts a cinema outing where Valentine and Leeza watch a film, visit the concessions stand, and share a playful moment with a boy. The passage ends abruptly as the next picture is shut off.
one_line: Valentine and friends recall the zombie-driven revolution taught through a game, then enjoy a cinema outing before it abruptly ends.
key_facts: The revolution was taught to Valentine through a game that she played quite a lot and thought was quite good.
The game featured a virtual city modeled on Valentine's own city, along with combat sequences and scary zombies.
Zombiism and the need to cure it had outweighed every other priority before the revolution.
Three governments had promised to negotiate better prices for zombiism drugs and had failed.
The Cabinet was overrun by zombies who tore three MPs to bits and infected seven more.
The crowd carried the PM out of her office, put her in a barrel, drove nails through it, and rolled it into the river.
The new PM built zombiism drug factories in the city, giving away the drug in spray, pill and needle forms.
After the revolution, copies of movies, songs, drugs, buildings and cars were made right there in the city.
Valentine and Leeza, who was her best friend that week, watched a movie together with their arms around each other's shoulders.
The movie was about a woman in love with two men who hated each other, and the audio was dubbed over from English.
The cinema was celebrating its opening day with chocolates, brown beer for adults, and bottles of fizzy elderflower for kids.
Valentine tripped a cute boy whom Leeza liked, so he nearly fell into Leeza's lap.
The next picture barely had time to start before it was shut off.
